## Minimum attainable p-value for this design

<a id="minimum-attainable-p-for-design"></a>

**When:** can this test even reach significance with so few runs  
**Tier:** `INLINE`  
**Earns its place by:** encodes a fact the agent has no way to know it doesn't know

```
python3 models/design/minimum_attainable_p_for_design.py --n1 N --n2 N   |   --pairs N   [--alpha 0.05] [--sided 2]
```

**Returns:** smallest p the design can produce, and whether alpha is reachable at all

**Also asked as:**

- is my sample too small to prove anything
- three runs each, can I get a p value
- why can't I get a significant result from this comparison
- before and after on five items, is that enough

**Refuses (exit 3) when:** a group size below 1, both designs given at once, or alpha outside (0,1)

*Why it exists:* No recorded baseline in evals/baselines/ mentioned the attainability floor. Encodes a fact rather than a computation.

## Benchmark runs needed per arm

<a id="benchmark-runs-needed"></a>

**When:** how many times should I run this benchmark  
**Tier:** `MUST-CONSTRUCT-DATA`  
**Earns its place by:** encodes a fact the agent has no way to know it doesn't know

```
python3 models/design/benchmark_runs_needed.py --effect DELTA (--sd SD | --pilot v1,v2,...) [--power 0.8] [--alpha 0.05]
```

**Returns:** runs per arm needed; with --pilot, widened for uncertainty in the sd estimate

**Must beat:** the conventional default of 30 runs per arm — if it does not, the script prints that answer instead and exits 5.

**Also asked as:**

- how many samples do I need to detect a slowdown
- is five runs enough to tell if it got slower
- how much data do I need before I can decide
- planning a performance comparison, what sample size

**Refuses (exit 3) when:** effect not positive, neither or both of --sd/--pilot, fewer than 2 pilot values, or zero pilot spread

**Unanswerable (exit 4) when:** the required runs exceed what any workflow could execute, meaning the effect is not measurable against this noise

**Hazard:** Do not feed the same pilot runs into the comparison you are sizing. Reusing them makes the test optimistic; collect fresh runs.

**Requires of the data:** pilot runs must be interleaved or randomised, not all-old-then-all-new; sequential collection makes the sd estimate reflect drift rather than noise

**Requires independence:** observations must not share a generator. Repeated runs of one process, or several agents querying one model, are not independent observations.

*Why it exists:* Baseline S1 computed a correct Welch t-test on 5 runs and never asked how many were needed; it scored 3/4 for that omission.
